abstract: The continuous deployment of enterprise voice systems creates a critical operational bottleneck: evaluating the acoustic quality of synthetic speech across high-volume production updates. While human Mean Opinion Score (MOS) remains the quality gold standard, it introduces severe operational costs and turn-around delays that make continuous integration infeasible. In this work, we present a system design case study for a scalable, low-cost and offline evaluation pipeline capable of scoring large batches of synthetic speech at marginal cost. First, we use Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct in a zero-shot setting for granular MOS estimation, noticing perceptual blind spots and inherent biases. Then, we analyze SOMOS dataset and construct a diagnostic benchmark that operationalizes two prosodic dimensions associated with human naturalness ratings. Finally, we adapt Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct through a parameter-efficient finetuning (LoRA) on the task of MOS evaluation, observing improvements over base model and widely used neural baselines like UTMOS and establishing a practical blueprint for enterprise-grade speech quality assurance.

oneSentenceThesis: 本文以 Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct 为对象，先证明零样本提示无法可靠预测 MOS，再用 SOMOS 数据诊断其语速与表现力感知盲区，最后用 4 比特量化下单卡 LoRA 微调把 Pearson 相关从接近 0 提升到 0.6506 并超过 UTMOSv2，代价是结论只在英语合成语音的域内测试上成立。
originalTitle: Scalable Audio-LLM System for Speech MOS Evaluation: A Diagnostic Case Study and Adaptation Roadmap
readerTitle: 让音频大模型学会打分：语音 MOS 自动评估的诊断与适配
